subject: C41
required_fixes: R1 — apps/desktop/src/v2/workbench/api-client.tsx:178–188, especially the doc.id shortcut at line 186: returning to a request can remount an obsolete DocumentView. RequestEditor owns newer fields/revisions internally, while the parent retains its original document. Reproduced against the production component in memory: edit A's URL, receive successful protection, select B and lose its load observation, then select A. The URL reverted from /edited to /topics and A had only one openRequest call. Save can then remove the protected draft because those old fields equal the saved baseline (workbench_domain.rs:1828–1839); Send can use the old request. Reload the authoritative document when returning after its editor unmounts, or retain an up-to-date document without reviving an obsolete snapshot. Acceptance: regression tests cover A edited/protected or saved, B's load pending/refused/undelivered, and return to A; latest fields and revision survive and explicit Save/Send receive them, with no automatic send.

R2 — apps/desktop/src/v2/workbench/tools-sheet.tsx:242 and 251: schema-open replies unconditionally replace the editor even after a newer editor action. Reproduced against ToolsSheet in memory: hold openSchema(existing.json), create draft.json, type {"newWork":true}, then release the old result. The draft editor disappeared and was replaced by existing.json's text; the unsaved work was lost. Bind loads to the current editor generation and retire them on New, Close, or another selection. The environment loader at lines 94–102 has the same unguarded replacement pattern and needs equivalent protection. Acceptance: deferred opens superseded by a new schema, closing the editor, or a newer environment/schema selection cannot reopen or replace the current editor or its typing; add component regressions alongside the save-reply tests.
